mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 1.0% signals monetary tightening, which raises discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When CPI inflation exceeds 245.0, it signals persistent price pressures that may trigger short-term economic optimism about growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 245.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in employment (PAYEMS) and fall in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in less than 50% of instances when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals robust demand for housing and related sectors, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in less than 50% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST rises, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 indicates weakening supply chain activity and economic contraction, reducing corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 105.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) fall below 470,000 million dollars, it signals a contraction in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 50% of instances when RSAFS < 470000, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate above 1.0% and CPI inflation above 245.0 indicates aggressive monetary tightening in response to high inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 50% of instances when both FEDFUNDS > 1.0 and CPIAUCSL > 245.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During post-recession recovery, a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals improving labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in less than 50% of instances during post-recession recovery when UNRATE declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
